input: Sign up for a wilderness survival skills weekend

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Survival skills span a wide range — fire-making, shelter, navigation, foraging, first aid, water sourcing — knowing which skills the user wants to focus on determines which courses are relevant.
Whether this is for the user alone, with a partner, family, or a group changes course type, group size requirements, and registration logistics.
The geographic region or preferred location (terrain type, proximity to home) directly filters which specific courses are accessible and realistic.
Budget is a hard filter — wilderness survival weekends range from ~$100 community workshops to $1,000+ professional schools, so knowing the ceiling rules options in or out immediately.
Experience level (complete beginner vs. some outdoors background) determines whether an intro course or an intermediate/advanced programme is the right fit.
The user's underlying goal — general preparedness, a specific trip, a hobby, professional certification — shapes what 'a good course' looks like and which credentials or outcomes matter.
Target timeframe (a specific upcoming weekend, within the next month, flexible) determines urgency, how much research time exists, and whether waitlists are a concern.

gold.taskTitle: Sign up for a wilderness survival skills weekend
gold.taskDescription: Find and register for a weekend course or camp that teaches hands-on wilderness survival skills.

questions.title: Which survival skills do you most want to learn?
questions.description: Identify the specific skills of highest interest — e.g., fire-starting, shelter-building, water sourcing, navigation, foraging, wilderness first aid — to filter courses by curriculum.

questions.title: Is this just for you or a group?
questions.description: Determine whether registration is for one person, a couple, a family with children, or a larger group, as this affects course eligibility and booking requirements.

questions.title: What region or terrain type do you want?
questions.description: Establish the preferred location — near home, a specific state or country, a particular environment like mountains, forest, or desert — to narrow down geographically viable options.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for the course?
questions.description: Set a clear spending ceiling (covering course fees, gear, travel, and accommodation if not included) to eliminate options outside the feasible range immediately.

questions.title: How would you describe your current outdoors experience level?
questions.description: Gauge whether the user is a complete beginner, casually experienced, or has prior survival training, so the course difficulty and pace are a good match.

questions.title: What is your main reason for wanting this training?
questions.description: Clarify the driving goal — general preparedness, an upcoming expedition, a personal challenge, professional certification, or pure interest — to prioritise the most relevant course outcomes.

questions.title: When do you want to attend — any specific dates in mind?
questions.description: Pin down the target timeframe (a fixed weekend, within the next 1–3 months, fully flexible) to assess urgency and check availability or waitlists accordingly.
